text:
incbot: INCIDENT P1 - network-egress-degradation in azure-brazilsouth. Multiple Private deployments reporting DNS resolution stalls and elevated token latency. Paging on-call.

alice-oncall: acked. I’m oncall for infra. Initial triage: customers on private VNet + ExpressRoute peering to on-prem are seeing intermittent DNS NXDOMAINs and long DNS query latencies. Symptoms starting ~07:40 BRT.

mike-netops: adding context from cloud: Azure reports peering route suppressions around brazilsouth regional fabric, multiple route flaps observed on MS-side. We’re seeing a transit path shift that forces DNS to take a longer on-prem detour.

sara-sre: Assigning incident commander. I’ll take IC and coordinate mitigations. @alice-oncall please keep collecting packet captures/traceroutes from affected customer gateways.

alice-oncall: on it. I’ve asked 2 affected customers for tcpdump and traceroute. Also collecting vnet peering status. Example commands I ran:
```
# check local DNS latency
dig +time=2 +tries=2 @10.0.0.2 model-api.customer.example.com
# azure vnet gateway
az network vnet-gateway show -g rg-prod --name rg-prod-vpngw
``` 

jordan-support: customers reporting 502s and model timeouts in Private deployments (low volume, high severity). We have 3 active support tickets and 5 automated customer alerts.

sara-sre: Severity P1 confirmed. Impact: Private inference endpoints in brazilsouth experiencing failed requests or >3x p99 latency. Hosted (public) endpoints not widely affected. Note: this impacts on-prem-connected customers using Private deployment with ExpressRoute/VPN.

amanda-pm: Preparing customer comms. Need ETA for mitigation and workaround. Which service config can we flip quickly? :eyes:

mike-netops: Short-term options: 1) Force smart-routing fallback to an alternate region for affected tenants (we can update routing policy in the control plane). 2) Push DNS fallback to global resolver (short TTL). 3) Ask customers to fail over to dedicated region (manual) as A/B.

sara-sre: Plan: enact control-plane routing override for affected customer tags to route inference traffic to azure-southcentral-fallback for 1 hour to stabilize. This preserves session affinity where possible. Simultaneously shorten DNS TTLs for private endpoints to 30s to allow quick client failover. Rollback plan in 30m if no regressions.

alice-oncall: I’ll prepare the change. Pushing a staging config now to test on a single tenant.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by alice-oncall: route-override/216 -> in progress (CI build 4398)

alice-oncall: test tenant shows immediate drop in p99 latency from 2.3s -> 320ms. Logs: fewer DNS timeouts. Good sign.

sara-sre: Proceeding to roll to affected tenants in batches of 10. @jordan-support please update the three customer tickets with "temporary routing fallback in progress" and expected 15-30m stabilization window.

jordan-support: updating tickets now. Sending proactive note to top 10 affected customers. Template: "We observed regional network instability impacting private endpoints in Azure Brazilsouth. We're routing your traffic to a fallback region; you may see a brief reconnection. We'll update when stable." :envelope_with_arrow:

mike-netops: While routing override is rolled out, we should collect BGP updates and Azure peering logs. Asking MS support to escalate for fabric route flap analysis. I’ve opened ticket with Azure (SR 2026-8421).

sara-sre: Agreed. Also setting up a call with the top 3 customers if they need support migrating workloads.

alice-oncall: rollout batch 1/4 completed. Metrics: successful requests up 28%, DNS NXDOMAINs down to normal levels for those tenants.

deploy-bot: deploy completed route-override/216 -> success

sara-sre: Good. Moving to batch 2. ETA for full rollback depends on Azure fabric stabilization. If Azure fixes within 1h we’ll revert route override. If not, plan for extended fallback and update pricing/latency advisory.

amanda-pm: Preparing external status: "Partial outage for Private deployments in Azure Brazilsouth. Temporary fallback routing in effect. No action required; customer impact limited to elevated request latency for a subset of requests." Will post to status.redwood shortly.

jordan-support: status update posted. Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2155551234

mike-netops: Azure responded: they are seeing control-plane fabric microloop causing route churn due to a failed spine update; fix in progress but no ETA. They recommend our temporary routing/fallback.

sara-sre: Continuing monitoring. Action items:
- alice-oncall: finish rollout and monitor p99 and errors (DORA: latency + 5xx)
- mike-netops: maintain SR with Azure and push for timeline
- jordan-support: continue customer updates every 30m
- amanda-pm: prepare post-incident RCA draft

alice-oncall: rollout 4/4 done. All affected tenants now on fallback. System p99 for Private endpoints in brazilsouth region now within normal range with increased regional egress costs.

jordan-support: customers acknowledged the proactive action, 2 on-call CTAs requested support migrating their dedicated routing permanently — flagged for account teams.

sara-sre: Great. Monitoring window started. If no new flaps in next 45m, we’ll begin coordinated rollback. Keep SR open and collect timestamps for RCA.

mike-netops: collected BGP dumps and Azure peering logs attached in the incident doc. Also note: DNS authoritative path had a split-brain where queries to regional resolver sometimes hit stale NS set, producing NXDOMAINs. We captured dig traces:
```
; dig trace example
dig +trace model-api.customer.example.com @10.0.0.2
; results: intermittent NXDOMAIN from region resolver, global resolver returns A records
```

incbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: routing override completed. Severity remains P1 until rollback verified. Next update in 30m or on significant change.

sara-sre: After 45m monitoring, system stable. Azure reports partial repair, but peering fabric still shows residual route churn. Decision: keep fallback for 2 hours, then do staged rollback with canary tenant.

amanda-pm: Noting customer impact for billing/incident report. We’ll include latency delta and tokens lost in postmortem.

jordan-support: Final customer note scheduled for 2 hours; immediate notes sent. Customers asking about causality and permanent mitigation.

sara-sre: Postmortem outline: timeline, root cause (Azure fabric route churn -> DNS path asymmetry -> NXDOMAINs), mitigations performed (control-plane routing override, DNS TTL reduction), metrics, follow-ups with Azure, recommended platform changes (automated cross-region fallback for Private tenants, clearer SLAs on cross-region egress), owners assigned.

alice-oncall: handing off to night oncall at 2155557000. @sara-sre remains IC. Leaving monitoring dashboard and runbook links in the incident doc.

sara-sre: Thanks @alice-oncall. Closing active rollouts. If anything flares up, page primary SRE. Incident remains open for RCA until Azure confirms full fabric repair.

incbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring) - routing override in place, customer impact mitigated. Update: incident will move to postmortem phase. Tags: azure, network, dns, private-deployments, paging.
